findings.title: Judge model: Fig 2/3 (all_models, 36 logs) and habench (20) are graded by openai/gpt-4.1, SnitchBench (8) by claude-sonnet-4; the paper (3.4) and our research note say GPT-5
findings.check: L1-05 grader facet, L2 identity (judge actors)
findings.evidence: task_args.params.grader_model: gpt-5 108 logs (0_baseline, 1-5_*), gpt-4.1 68 (0_baseline_gpt_4.1_grader 12, all_models 36, habench 20), snitchbench task_args.grader_model claude-sonnet-4-20250514 8. AER judge actors (model events in scorer spans) agree in all 7,700 sampled executions: all_models 1,800 gpt-4.1, habench 1,000 gpt-4.1, snitchbench 400 claude-sonnet-4. The paper's headline Fig 2/3 counts reproduce exactly (54/54) from these GPT-4.1-judged logs, so the published bars rest on a GPT-4.1 judge.
findings.reproduction: uv run python -I docs/reports/precheck/data/whistlebench/exam-scripts/raw.py (params_by_experiment in raw-census.json); uv run python -I docs/reports/precheck/data/whistlebench/exam-scripts/aer_pass.py (judge_models_by_experiment)
findings.recommendation: Disclose in the corpus datasheet: judge per experiment as recorded (gpt-5 / gpt-4.1 / claude-sonnet-4). Correct research.json/prereg judge line (R4, owner this pre-check). Identity: the engine already names the judge model per execution (no change).

verdicts.reasoning: Paper section 3.4 (arXiv v3) names GPT-5 as the LLM judge for the main results; the 36 all_models logs record grader_model openai/gpt-4.1 and the AER judge actors (from scorer-span model events) agree, 1,800/1,800; Fig 2/3 cells reproduce 54/54 from these logs, so the figure's logs are these. The pinned code default is openai/gpt-5 (whistlebench/types.py) and all_models.py does not set a grader, so the code also disagrees with the logs. SnitchBench logs judged by claude-sonnet-4 (paper names no judge for Fig 7). Headline figure method: S2 per R3. Side note (R4, not a new finding): the profile quirk note lists only gpt-4.1/gpt-5 judges, not claude-sonnet-4.
